capabilities: capture session log entries with time, tags and wiki links
create new session notes linked to the previous session
log combat events from Quick Initiative automatically
log dice rolls from Dice Tray into the session log
log clock ticks from Tabletop Clocks into the session log
disambiguation: Not an initiative tracker or dice roller itself; it only writes log entries, fights, rolls and clocks recorded by other plugins.
extras: Works entirely offline with no accounts. Part of a suite of TTRPG plugins by the same maker (Mapsmith, Quick Initiative, Dice Tray, Encounter Builder, Tabletop Clocks, DM Screen, Solo Oracle); DM Screen is paid. Manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. A browser demo is available to try before installing.
problem: Game masters struggle to capture what happens at the table in the moment, so session recaps are hard to write after the game.

relations.evidence: With Quick Initiative installed, fights log themselves
With Dice Tray installed, a roll you click goes into the log
With Tabletop Clocks installed, every clock you tick goes into the log too

summary: Session logger for tabletop games that turns typed lines into a timestamped, tagged Markdown list inside a session-log block in your session note.
